title: Introduction to the GraphExperiment class
text: Networks (graphs) become widely used data representations biology, can efficiently encode node-node interactions neighborhoods. high-throughput, quantitative omics data (e.g., transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, etc), widely used feature-level network representations include gene coexpression, protein-protein interaction, gene regulatory, co-abundance networks, cell-cell communication, sample-sample similarity, species-species networks observation level. data structures store quantitative data associated metadata exist (e.g., SummarizedExperiment, SingleCellExperiment, SpatialExperiment, etc), support networks describing features (.e., assay rows) /observations (.e., assay columns) relate currently missing. GraphExperiment S4 class extends SingleCellExperiment (Amezquita et al. 2020) include additional containers networks associated assay features (rowGraphs) assay observations (colGraphs). note, trees alternative way representing assay features/observations related . Users interested tree representations assays rows/columns can use TreeSummarizedExperiment package. Trees essentially kind graph (.e., trees graphs, graphs trees). , chose use general graph representation (namely igraph objects) provide users developers flexibility.

title: Introduction to the GraphExperiment class
text: Since GraphExperiment class extends SingleCellExperiment class, SingleCellExperiment slots present GraphExperiment, including: assays: list matrices primary (e.g., counts) transformed (e.g., log-normalized counts, TPM, etc) data, features rows observations columns. colData: data frame column (observation) metadata, cell type, sample ID, condition, batch ID, genotype, etc. rowData: data frame row (feature) metadata, gene ID, genomic coordinates, functional annotation, etc. reducedDims: list data frames reduced dimensions, PCA, t-SNE, UMAP embeddings. Compared SingleCellExperiment objects, GraphExperiment provides two additional containers: 1 rowGraphs: list igraph objects containing graphs representing feature-feature relationships, including (optional) node edge attributes. colGraphs: list igraph objects containing graphs representing observation-observation relationships, including (optional) node edge attributes. GraphExperiment class. igraph data class igraph package standard data structure graph representation R. unfamiliar igraph objects, can learn reading igraph vignettes.

title: Introduction to the GraphExperiment class
text: GraphExperiment objects can created scratch using constructor function GraphExperiment(). simulate scRNA-seq count matrix gene (row) cell (column) metadata, create graphs based gene-gene cell-cell correlations 2. create GraphExperiment object constructor function, run: ’re familiar SummarizedExperiment SingleCellExperiment objects, certainly recognize nearly everything see ge. Compared SingleCellExperiment objects, difference last two rows, indicate object contains rowGraph named ‘gene_cor’ colGraph named ‘cell_cor’. Importantly, since nodes rowGraphs/colGraphs always sync rownames/colnames, feature IDs rownames rowGraphs must , likewise observation IDs colnames colGraphs. example, attempting create GraphExperiment object features rownames missing lead error: Alternatively, can create GraphExperiment object coercing existing (Ranged)SummarizedExperiment SingleCellExperiment object. example: Note rowGraphs/colGraphs containers still , empty. access names graphs, use rowGraphNames() colGraphNames() functions.
code: # Simulate parts of a `GraphExperiment` object ## Assays gene_ids <- paste0("gene", seq_len(200)) cell_ids <- paste0("cell", seq_len(100)) mat <- matrix(rpois(20000, 5), ncol = 100, dimnames = list(gene_ids, cell_ids)) mat[1:5, 1:5] #>       cell1 cell2 cell3 cell4 cell5 #> gene1     6     7     5     5     6 #> gene2     5     3     6     3     5 #> gene3     4     5     9     7     2 #> gene4    12     4     5     9     3 #> gene5     6     6     5     2     8  ## rowData rdata <- data.frame(     row.names = gene_ids,     pathway = sample(c("P1", "P2"), size = length(gene_ids), replace = TRUE),     coding = sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = length(gene_ids), replace = TRUE) ) head(rdata) #>       pathway coding #> gene1      P1  FALSE #> gene2      P1   TRUE #> gene3      P2   TRUE #> gene4      P1  FALSE #> gene5      P1   TRUE #> gene6      P1  FALSE  ## colData cdata <- data.frame(     row.names = cell_ids,      cell_type = sample(c("ct1", "ct2"), size = length(cell_ids), replace = TRUE) ) head(cdata) #>       cell_type #> cell1       ct2 #> cell2       ct2 #> cell3       ct2 #> cell4       ct1 #> cell5       ct2 #> cell6       ct1  ## rowGraph (with node attribute `degree`) rg <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(     cor(t(mat)), mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE ) rg <- set_vertex_attr(rg, "degree", value = strength(rg)) rg #> IGRAPH c8329f2 UNW- 200 20096 --  #> + attr: name (v/c), degree (v/n), weight (e/n) #> + edges from c8329f2 (vertex names): #>  [1] gene1--gene1  gene1--gene2  gene1--gene3  gene1--gene4  gene1--gene5  #>  [6] gene1--gene6  gene1--gene7  gene1--gene8  gene1--gene9  gene1--gene10 #> [11] gene1--gene11 gene1--gene12 gene1--gene13 gene1--gene14 gene1--gene15 #> [16] gene1--gene16 gene1--gene17 gene1--gene18 gene1--gene19 gene1--gene20 #> [21] gene1--gene21 gene1--gene22 gene1--gene23 gene1--gene24 gene1--gene25 #> [26] gene1--gene26 gene1--gene27 gene1--gene28 gene1--gene29 gene1--gene30 #> [31] gene1--gene31 gene1--gene32 gene1--gene33 gene1--gene34 gene1--gene35 #> [36] gene1--gene36 gene1--gene37 gene1--gene38 gene1--gene39 gene1--gene40 #> + ... omitted several edges  ## colGraph cg <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(     cor(mat), mode = "undirected", weighted = TRUE ) # Create a `GraphExperiment` object ge <- GraphExperiment(     assays = list(counts = mat),     rowData = rdata,     colData = cdata,     rowGraphs = list(gene_cor = rg),     colGraphs = list(cell_cor = cg) ) ge #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(3): pathway coding gene_cor__degree #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(1): cell_type #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> rowGraphs(1): gene_cor #> colGraphs(1): cell_cor # Remove 'gene1' to 'gene10' from the rowGraph and try to recreate object rg2 <- delete_vertices(rg, paste0("gene", 1:10)) GraphExperiment(     assays = list(counts = mat),     rowData = rdata,     colData = cdata,     rowGraphs = list(gene_cor = rg2) ) #> Error in `validObject()`: #> ! invalid class "GraphExperiment" object:  #>     10 feature(s) in 'rownames' are missing from graph 'gene_cor'. # Coercing from `SummarizedExperiment` se <- SummarizedExperiment(list(counts = mat)) ge1 <- as(se, "GraphExperiment") ge1 #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(0): #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(0): #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> rowGraphs(0): #> colGraphs(0): # Get rowGraph names rowGraphNames(ge)      # 'gene_cor' #> [1] "gene_cor" rowGraphNames(ge1)     # empty (NULL) #> NULL  # Get colGraph names colGraphNames(ge)      # 'cell_cor' #> [1] "cell_cor" colGraphNames(ge1)     # empty (NULL) #> NULL

code: # Create a new rowGraph without correlations between -0.4 and 0.4 rg_filt <- rowGraph(ge, "gene_cor") |>      delete_vertex_attr("pathway") |>     delete_vertex_attr("degree") |>     delete_vertex_attr("coding")  todelete <- abs(E(rg_filt)$weight) <0.4 rg_filt <- delete_edges(rg_filt, which(todelete)) rg_filt #> IGRAPH 7c25d9b UNW- 200 202 --  #> + attr: name (v/c), weight (e/n) #> + edges from 7c25d9b (vertex names): #>  [1] gene1 --gene1  gene2 --gene2  gene3 --gene3  gene4 --gene4  gene5 --gene5  #>  [6] gene6 --gene6  gene7 --gene7  gene8 --gene8  gene9 --gene9  gene10--gene10 #> [11] gene11--gene11 gene12--gene12 gene13--gene13 gene14--gene14 gene15--gene15 #> [16] gene16--gene16 gene17--gene17 gene18--gene18 gene19--gene19 gene20--gene20 #> [21] gene21--gene21 gene22--gene22 gene23--gene23 gene24--gene24 gene25--gene25 #> [26] gene26--gene26 gene27--gene27 gene28--gene28 gene29--gene29 gene30--gene30 #> [31] gene31--gene31 gene32--gene32 gene33--gene33 gene34--gene34 gene35--gene35 #> [36] gene36--gene36 gene37--gene37 gene38--gene38 gene39--gene39 gene40--gene40 #> + ... omitted several edges  # Add filtered graph a new graph named `fcor` rowGraph(ge, "filt_genecor") <- rg_filt ge #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(3): pathway coding gene_cor__degree #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(1): cell_type #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> rowGraphs(2): gene_cor filt_genecor #> colGraphs(1): cell_cor # Taking a quick look (note: nothing in `rowGraphs`/`colGraphs`) ge1 #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(0): #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(0): #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> rowGraphs(0): #> colGraphs(0):  # Adding graphs from `ge` rowGraphs(ge1) <- rowGraphs(ge) colGraphs(ge1) <- colGraphs(ge) ge1 #> class: GraphExperiment  #> dim: 200 100  #> metadata(0): #> assays(1): counts #> rownames(200): gene1 gene2 ... gene199 gene200 #> rowData names(5): gene_cor__degree gene_cor__pathway gene_cor__coding #>   filt_genecor__pathway filt_genecor__coding #> colnames(100): cell1 cell2 ... cell99 cell100 #> colData names(1): cell_cor__cell_type #> reducedDimNames(0): #> mainExpName: NULL #> altExpNames(0): #> rowGraphs(2): gene_cor filt_genecor #> colGraphs(1): cell_cor # title: GraphExperiment S4 class — GraphExperiment-class
text: Like SingleCellExperiment, GraphExperiment S4 class stores quantitative data associated metadata (.e., rowData colData) along embeddings dimensionality reduction techniques. However, provides users additional containers igraph objects containing graphs describing features /observations interact . Graphs features stored rowGraphs slot, graphs observations stored colGraphs slot. slots can hold one multiple igraph objects sort network representation features rownames observations colnames. Example graphs features can coexpression networks, regulatory networks, co-abundance networks. Example graphs observations can cell-cell distances, sample-sample distances, species networks representing genealogies (alternative phylogenies). Importantly, node names row graph must match rownames assays, node names column graph must match colnames assays. Besides, subsetting methods simultaneously subset assays, rowData, rowGraphs, colData, colGraphs. Besides constructor function (GraphExperiment()), GraphExperiment object can also created coercing SummarizedExperiment SingleCellExperiment object.
